title: The impact of burnout and depression on sexual functioning and satisfaction among physicians: A cross-sectional study
summary:
Physicians in Germany are frequently exposed to high levels of occupational stress, which may be associated with an increased risk of burnout and depressive symptoms. Psychological stress and mental health conditions are also associated with impairments in sexual functioning and satisfaction. Since sexual health is an important component of quality of life, it is relevant to further investigate these associations among physicians.

The aim of this study is to investigate the association between work-related psychological stress and sexual health among physicians in Germany. The primary focus is on whether and to what extent burnout symptoms and depressive symptoms are associated with impairments in sexual functioning and reduced sexual satisfaction.

Data will be collected through an anonymous online survey.
conditions: Burnout symptoms, depression, impairments in sexual functioning, and sexual satisfaction

interventions.name: Physicians in Germany will be surveyed once via an online questionnaire about burnout and depressive symptoms, as well as their sexual functioning and satisfaction.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Licensed physicians in Germany
- Clinical or outpatient practice
- Working at least 50% of full-time hours
Exclusion criteria:
- Known organic sexual dysfunction
- Medication known to affect sexual function
- Current psychotherapy
- Pregnancy
